options.text: All birds acquiring the same inherited beak in one day

questions.explanation: Differential reproduction can raise the frequency of a heritable trait. It does not require individuals to decide how their genes change.

questions.stem: Two Aa parents have two children independently. Exactly one child shows the recessive trait. What is the probability that the other child is a carrier?
questions.explanation: The other child shows the dominant trait. Among its three equally likely dominant outcomes AA, Aa and aA, two are carriers. Knowing the sibling’s genotype does not change those probabilities.

questions.stem: A diagram shows a red blood cell moving through first a lung capillary and then a capillary beside an actively respiring muscle. Where does the cell tend to load and unload oxygen?

options.label: A
options.text: It binds to haemoglobin at the muscle and is released at the lung.

options.label: B
options.text: It stays bound to haemoglobin in both locations.

options.label: C
options.text: It binds to haemoglobin at the lung and is released near the muscle.

options.label: D
options.text: It is carried mainly by the cell’s nucleus and released near the muscle.

options.label: E
options.text: It is made by the cell at the lung and destroyed at the muscle.

questions.explanation: Haemoglobin loads oxygen where oxygen concentration is high in the lungs and releases it where the concentration is lower near respiring tissues.

questions.stem: What helps maintain a steep oxygen concentration gradient across the wall of an alveolus?

options.label: A
options.text: Oxygen is never moved away from the capillary.

options.label: B
options.text: Ventilation replenishes oxygen in its air and blood flow removes absorbed oxygen.

options.label: C
options.text: Ventilation blocks fresh air from reaching it.

options.label: D
options.text: The alveolar wall becomes very thick.

options.label: E
options.text: Oxygen levels on both sides become permanently equal.

questions.explanation: Ventilation and perfusion continuously renew the two sides of the exchange surface, maintaining the gradient.

questions.stem: A person is hot and sweating, but the sweat cannot evaporate. Why is cooling reduced?

options.label: A
options.text: Sweat can only cool by raising blood glucose.

options.label: B
options.text: Liquid sweat must produce heat by respiration.

options.label: C
options.text: Air can cool only by entering the bloodstream.

options.label: D
options.text: Sweat becomes more acidic and stops heat transfer entirely.

options.label: E
options.text: Less energy is transferred away by evaporation.

questions.explanation: Evaporation removes energy from the skin. Producing sweat without evaporation gives less of that cooling effect.

questions.stem: Heart rate is 60 beats/min with 80 mL ejected per beat, then 100 beats/min with 60 mL per beat. Which row gives the two cardiac outputs in L/min?
questions.explanation: Multiply each rate by its matching stroke volume, then divide mL/min by 1000.

questions.stem: Person X drinks water and later produces 400 mL of dilute urine. Person Y produces 200 mL of urine with twice its solute concentration. Assuming equal time windows, what follows about amounts of solute excreted?

options.label: C
options.text: Y excretes four times X’s amount.

options.label: D
options.text: Both excrete the same amount in those windows.

questions.explanation: Amount is concentration multiplied by volume. Y’s doubled concentration is offset by half the volume.

questions.stem: A villus model absorbs a dissolved substance by diffusion. The liquid outside the villus stays fixed in concentration. Inside, liquid is either replaced continuously or left stagnant. Which pattern is expected?

options.label: A
options.text: The stagnant model speeds up as the inside concentration rises.

options.label: B
options.text: Both models keep exactly the same gradient indefinitely.

options.label: C
options.text: Replacement must reverse the direction of diffusion.

options.label: D
options.text: The stagnant model slows as inside concentration rises; replacement helps maintain the gradient.

options.label: E
options.text: The models differ only because diffusion requires ATP.

questions.explanation: In the stagnant model, uptake raises the inside concentration and reduces the difference across the wall. Replacement carries absorbed material away, as blood flow does.

questions.stem: When blood glucose is low, which pattern supports a return towards normal? Give the hormone followed by the relevant liver response.

options.label: E
options.text: Insulin; conversion of glucose to starch

options.label: F
options.text: Glucagon; active removal of glucose from blood

options.label: G
options.text: Both hormones; complete cessation of metabolism

questions.explanation: Glucagon promotes glycogen breakdown and glucose release, which raises low blood glucose.

questions.stem: Touching a sharp object triggers withdrawal before conscious processing of pain. Which feature enables that order?

options.label: A
options.text: The spinal cord coordinates the motor response without waiting for conscious processing.

options.label: B
options.text: The sensory neurone travels directly into the muscle without entering the central nervous system.

options.label: C
options.text: The muscles signal the skin before it detects the stimulus.

options.label: D
options.text: All reflex messages travel only in blood.

options.label: E
options.text: The brain blocks every motor signal until it detects pain.

questions.explanation: A withdrawal reflex can use a spinal circuit. Conscious awareness can follow transmission to the brain.

questions.stem: Why does the left ventricle generally need thicker muscle than the right ventricle?

options.label: A
options.text: It sends blood only to the nearby lungs.

options.label: B
options.text: It contains no blood between contractions.

options.label: C
options.text: It pumps blood at higher pressure around the body.

options.label: D
options.text: It replaces the function of all arteries.

questions.explanation: Systemic circulation requires more pressure than the short pulmonary circuit. The left ventricle supplies the systemic route.

questions.stem: At rest an animal moves 5 L of blood each minute and extracts 5 mL O₂ per 100 mL blood. During activity flow is 8 L/min and extraction is 10 mL per 100 mL. By what factor does total oxygen extraction per minute increase?
questions.explanation: Total extraction scales with both flow and extraction per unit volume. The factors multiply to (8/5) × 2.

questions.stem: Part of a leaf is exposed to light, but the air contacting that part has had its carbon dioxide removed. The rest receives air containing carbon dioxide in otherwise identical conditions. Why is the first part expected to make less sugar?

options.label: A
options.text: It lacks oxygen for photosynthesis because no carbon dioxide is present.

options.label: B
options.text: It lacks the carbon dioxide that supplies carbon to photosynthesis.

options.label: C
options.text: It lacks the light energy required for photosynthesis.

options.label: D
options.text: Its water is converted into carbon dioxide instead of sugar.

options.label: E
options.text: Its chlorophyll cannot absorb light unless sugars arrive from the roots.

questions.explanation: Photosynthesis uses carbon dioxide as the carbon source for sugars. Both parts receive light, so reduced carbon dioxide availability explains the difference.

questions.stem: A shoot’s stomata close on a dry afternoon. What immediate effect on water vapour loss through its stomata is expected?

options.label: B
options.text: It becomes independent of all humidity differences.

options.label: C
options.text: Water vapour starts travelling down the xylem instead.

options.label: D
options.text: The phloem stops carrying carbon permanently.

questions.explanation: Closed pores reduce the route available for water vapour to diffuse out. Closing stomata does not turn the xylem into a gas channel.

questions.stem: In an isolated food chain of grass, rabbits and foxes, which organisms are primary consumers?
questions.explanation: Rabbits feed directly on the producer, grass. Foxes feed at the next trophic level.

questions.stem: Plants at identical light and temperature receive low or high CO₂. Net uptake is 3 and 9 units per hour respectively. Dark respiration releases 2 units per hour in both and is assumed unchanged in light. Which row gives the gross photosynthetic rates (low; high)?
questions.explanation: Net uptake is gross uptake minus 2 units lost in respiration. Add 2 to each measurement.

questions.stem: A student puts quadrats only close to a pond then uses them to estimate abundance across an entire field. The plant prefers wet ground. In which direction is the estimate most likely biased?

options.label: A
options.text: It is too low because wet ground always has fewer plants.

options.label: B
options.text: It is too high because sampling favours the plant’s preferred habitat.

options.label: C
options.text: It is unbiased because the quadrats are the same size.

options.label: D
options.text: It is unbiased because the plants are counted individually.

options.label: E
options.text: Its direction cannot be related to site choice even with the stated preference.

questions.explanation: Sampling only wet ground is likely to give a higher density than a representative field sample. Correct counting does not fix biased placement.

questions.stem: During a short interval plants fix 45 units of carbon, living organisms respire 27 units including 8 from decomposers, and a fire releases another 10 units. Considering these flows only, what is the change in atmospheric carbon?
questions.explanation: Photosynthesis removes 45 units and respiration and combustion return 27 + 10. The 8 from decomposers is already included in respiration.

questions.stem: A shoot takes up 16 mL water in an hour and stores 4 mL, with no other sinks than transpiration. Which row gives water transpired; percentage of uptake transpired?
questions.explanation: Subtract the stored amount from uptake. The 12 mL transpired is three quarters of the water absorbed.

questions.stem: In early spring a plant sends sucrose from root reserves to new shoots. Later, mature leaves send sucrose to the roots. What does this show about translocation?

options.label: A
options.text: Sucrose always moves in the same direction as water in xylem.

options.label: B
options.text: Mature leaves always act as sugar sinks.

options.label: C
options.text: The direction depends on which tissues supply and use sugars.

options.label: D
options.text: The roots can supply sucrose only after all leaves mature.

questions.explanation: The reserve acts as a source in spring and as a sink when mature leaves supply sugars. The source-to-sink direction need not stay fixed.

questions.stem: Prey eat 800 kJ per day. One quarter is unassimilated. Of the remainder, 450 kJ is used in respiration. Predators eat half the new prey biomass. What fraction of the original 800 kJ reaches the predators as food?
questions.explanation: The prey assimilate 600 kJ. After respiration 150 kJ goes to new biomass; predators eat half, and 75/800 simplifies to 3/32.

questions.stem: In a closed pond, 48 animals are marked and released. Later 40 are caught, of which 6 bear marks. If marked and unmarked animals are equally catchable and well mixed, what population estimate follows?
questions.explanation: Assume the marked fraction in the catch, 6/40, estimates the marked fraction of the whole pond. Divide 48 by 6/40.

questions.stem: Positive x satisfies x³ − 35x^(3/2) + 216 = 0. Find the sum of its possible values.
questions.explanation: Set t = x^(3/2). The quadratic factors as (t − 8)(t − 27), so x is 4 or 9. Add the values of x, not those of t.

questions.stem: An arithmetic sequence has partial sum Sₙ = 2n² + 3n. How many of its first nine terms exceed 19?
questions.explanation: The nth term is Sₙ − Sₙ₋₁ = 4n + 1. It exceeds 19 for n = 5 to 9; testing the partial sums instead counts the wrong quantities.

questions.stem: For which real x is √(4 − x²)/√(x − 1) defined?
questions.explanation: The numerator permits −2 ≤ x ≤ 2. The denominator must be real and nonzero, so x > 1. The intersection includes 2 but not 1.

questions.stem: Which expression equals √(13 + 4√10)?
questions.explanation: Squaring 2√2 + √5 gives 8 + 5 + 2(2√2)(√5) = 13 + 4√10. The positive sign also matters: √8 − √5 has the same rational part when squared but the opposite surd term.

questions.stem: Let u₁ = 0 and uₙ₊₁ = 2 − uₙ/2. How many of the first six terms exceed 4/3?
questions.explanation: Subtract the fixed point 4/3 from both sides to get uₙ₊₁ − 4/3 = −(uₙ − 4/3)/2. The sign alternates, so exactly the even terms among the first six exceed 4/3; the sequence does not approach the fixed point from one side.

questions.stem: A quadratic P(x) leaves the same remainder on division by x − 1 and x − 4. The equation P(x) = 7 has two real solutions. What is their sum?
questions.explanation: The remainder theorem gives P(1) = P(4), so the axis of symmetry is x = (1 + 4)/2. The two solutions are symmetric about that axis and sum to 5; 5/2 is their mean.

questions.stem: Solve (x − 2)² ≤ 2x + 1.
questions.explanation: Rearranging gives x² − 6x + 3 ≤ 0, or (x − 3)² ≤ 6. Equality is allowed, and the bound on the square gives the interval between the two roots, not the outside.

questions.stem: Both roots of x² + (k − 2)x + k = 0 are positive and unequal. Find the full range of k.
questions.explanation: A positive product and sum require k > 0 and 2 − k > 0. The discriminant k² − 8k + 4 is positive when k < 4 − 2√3 or k > 4 + 2√3, so intersecting with 0 < k < 2 gives the first interval. Equality at the upper limit gives a repeated root.

questions.stem: A convergent geometric series sums to 12. Its second, fourth, sixth, … terms sum to 4. What is its first term?
questions.explanation: The odd-numbered terms sum to 8, and multiplying each by r produces the corresponding even-numbered term. Hence r = 4/8 = 1/2 and the first term is 12(1 − r) = 6; 8 is the sum of all the odd-numbered terms.

questions.stem: The coefficient of x³ in (1 + 2x)⁵(1 − kx) is zero. Find k.
questions.explanation: The x³ coefficient of (1 + 2x)⁵ is 10 × 8 = 80, and its x² coefficient is 10 × 4 = 40. Multiplication gives 80 − 40k = 0, so k = 2; the second contribution uses the x² term, not the x³ term.

questions.stem: A line segment has endpoints (1, 2) and (7, 6). Possible sites for a transmitter are P(6, 1), Q(2, 7) and R(3, 6). Which sites are equidistant from the two endpoints?
questions.explanation: The perpendicular bisector passes through (4, 4) and has gradient −3/2. P and Q satisfy y − 4 = −3(x − 4)/2. At x = 3, the bisector has y = 5.5, not 6.

questions.stem: The circle (x + 3)² + (y − 2)² = 16 meets the x-axis at A and B. Find the product of their x-coordinates.
questions.explanation: At y = 0, (x + 3)² = 12. The product of −3 + √12 and −3 − √12 is 9 − 12.

questions.stem: The minimum of y = a(x + 3)² − 5 is −5 and the curve passes through (1, 3). Find its y-intercept.
questions.explanation: Using (1, 3) gives 16a = 8, hence a = 1/2. At x = 0 the curve has value 9/2 − 5, not −5.

questions.stem: Find the sum of the squares of the solutions to ∣x − 2∣ = 4 − x/2.
questions.explanation: Below 2, solve 2 − x = 4 − x/2; above 2, solve x − 2 = 4 − x/2. The valid solutions are −4 and 4, whose squares add rather than cancel.

questions.stem: The line y = −1 cuts (x − 1)² + (y − 2)² = 25 in a chord. Find the chord's length.
questions.explanation: Substituting y = −1 gives (x − 1)² = 16. The endpoints have x = 1 ± 4, so their separation is 8; 4 is only half the chord.

questions.stem: The only zeros of f are −1 and 4. What is the sum of the zeros of g(x) = f(3 − 2x)?
questions.explanation: Set 3 − 2x equal to each zero of f. This gives x = 2 and x = −1/2, with sum 3/2; applying 3 − 2x directly to the old zeros would transform in the wrong direction.

questions.stem: Real numbers x and y satisfy xy = 12 and y − x = 1. Find (x + y)².
questions.explanation: Use (x + y)² = (y − x)² + 4xy, giving 1 + 48 = 49. The sign of x + y can differ between solutions, but the square is fixed.

questions.stem: Tangents to (x − 1)² + (y + 2)² = 25 at (4, 2) and (5, 1) meet at P. Find the x-coordinate of P.
questions.explanation: The radii have gradients 4/3 and 3/4, so the tangent gradients are −3/4 and −4/3. The tangent equations are y = 5 − 3x/4 and y = 23/3 − 4x/3; equating gives x = 32/7. The midpoint of the contact points does not lie on both tangents.

questions.stem: For which k does |x² − 4| = k have exactly three distinct real solutions?
questions.explanation: For k > 0, the two equations are x² = 4 + k and x² = 4 − k. The first gives two roots and the second gives exactly one only when 4 − k = 0. At k = 0 the equations coincide, so their roots must not be counted twice.

questions.stem: How many real solutions does |x − 1| + |x + 2| = 3 have?
questions.explanation: For −2 ≤ x ≤ 1, the two terms are distances to the endpoints and sum to the interval length 3. Outside the interval their sum exceeds 3, so counting just the endpoints would miss all the solutions between them.

questions.stem: For acute θ, tan θ = sin(5π/6)/cos(π/6). Find sin(2θ).
questions.explanation: The ratio is 1/√3, so θ = π/6. Doubling the angle gives sin π/3 = √3/2; doubling sin θ would not give sin(2θ).

questions.stem: Solve log₄ x + log₈ x = 5/2 for x > 0.
questions.explanation: Let t = log₂ x. The left side is t/2 + t/3, so t = 3 and x = 2³. The logarithms cannot be merged by multiplication without first matching bases.

questions.stem: The curve y = 2 − 3(1/2)^x has horizontal asymptote y = 2. For what x is the curve one quarter of its x = 0 distance from that asymptote?
questions.explanation: The vertical gap is 3(1/2)^x, initially 3. Dividing the gap by 4 requires two halvings; do not divide the curve’s height by 4.

questions.stem: Two sides of a triangle are 4 and 6, with included angle 120°. Find the third side.
questions.explanation: The cosine rule gives c² = 4² + 6² − 2(4)(6)cos 120° = 76. Here the cosine is −1/2, so the last term increases the squared length; using +1/2 gives 2√7.

questions.stem: A circle has radius 6. Find the area of the minor segment cut off by a chord subtending π/3 at the centre.
questions.explanation: The sector has area ½ × 36 × π/3 = 6π. Subtract the triangle area ½ × 36 × sin(π/3) = 9√3; the segment is not the whole sector.

questions.stem: If tan θ = 2, find cos²θ − sin²θ.
questions.explanation: Since sin²θ = 4cos²θ and their sum is 1, the squared cosine and sine are 1/5 and 4/5. Subtract in the given order to get −3/5, not +3/5.

questions.stem: For x > 0, solve log₃(9/x) + log₃(x²) = 4.
questions.explanation: Combine the logarithms to obtain log₃(9x) = 4, so 9x = 81 and x = 9. Addition of logs corresponds to multiplication of their arguments, not addition.

questions.stem: How many solutions has cos(2x) = sin x on −π/2 ≤ x ≤ 3π/2?
questions.explanation: Using cos(2x) = 1 − 2sin²x gives (2sin x − 1)(sin x + 1) = 0. Sine equals 1/2 twice and equals −1 at both included endpoints, giving four distinct values of x; the endpoints differ by a full period but are distinct.
Squaring the given sum adds the cross term 2 × 2^x × 2^(−x) = 2. Subtract it from 25/4 to get 17/4; 25/4 is the square of the whole sum.

questions.stem: In a triangle ABC, A = 30°, BC = 5 and CA = 5√3. Two non-congruent triangles are possible. Find the sum of their areas.
questions.explanation: The sine rule gives sin B = √3/2, so B is 60° or 120° and C is 90° or 30°. The two sides enclosing C are 5 and 5√3, giving total area ½ × 25√3 × (1 + 1/2) = 75√3/4. Using only the acute value of B misses one of the triangles.

questions.stem: At two points on y = x³ + 2x² the tangents both have gradient 4. How far apart are their x-coordinates?
questions.explanation: Set the derivative 3x² + 4x equal to 4. The resulting quadratic has roots −2 and 2/3, whose separation is 8/3.

questions.stem: For x > 0, a curve has derivative 3x⁻² − 4x⁻³ and passes through (1, 2). Find its height at x = 2.
questions.explanation: An antiderivative is −3/x + 2/x². Its value is −1 at both x = 1 and x = 2, so the curve’s height is unchanged.

questions.stem: Let f(x) = x⁴ − 3x² + x. Find the sum of the squares of the real x-values where f″(x) = 0.
questions.explanation: Twice differentiating gives 12x² − 6, so both roots have square 1/2. Count both roots; squaring their sum would instead give zero.

questions.stem: The normal to y = √x at x = 4 crosses the y-axis at (0, c). Find c.
questions.explanation: The tangent gradient at x = 4 is 1/4, so the normal gradient is −4. Its line passes through (4, 2), giving c = 2 − (−4) × 4 = 18; the normal does not have the tangent slope.

questions.stem: Find the total area between y = x − 1 and the x-axis for 0 ≤ x ≤ 3.
questions.explanation: The graph crosses the axis at x = 1, making two triangles with areas 1/2 and 2. Add their magnitudes to get 5/2; the signed integral would subtract the lower triangle.

questions.stem: Given ∫₋₁³ f(x) dx = 7 and ∫₁³ f(x) dx = 2, find ∫₋₁¹ (2f(x) − 1) dx.
questions.explanation: Subtract the second integral from the first to get 5 on [−1, 1]. Doubling and subtracting the interval length 2 gives 8; integrating the constant −1 does not subtract just 1.

questions.stem: For y = (x² − 1)/√x, find dy/dx at x = 4.
questions.explanation: Write y = x^(3/2) − x^(−1/2), so dy/dx = (3/2)√x + (1/2)x^(−3/2). At 4 the value is 3 + 1/16 = 49/16; the negative coefficient and negative exponent make the second term of dy/dx positive.

questions.stem: Use two equal strips to estimate ∫₀² (x² + 1) dx by the trapezium rule. By how much does the estimate exceed the exact value?
questions.explanation: At x = 0, 1 and 2 the heights are 1, 2 and 5, so the estimate is (1 + 4 + 5)/2 = 5. The integral is 8/3 + 2 = 14/3, giving an excess of 1/3; the middle height counts twice.

questions.stem: For x > 0, dy/dx = 3x² − 4/x² and y(1) = 5. What is y(2)?
questions.explanation: Integrating gives y = x³ + 4/x + C. The initial value makes C = 0, so y(2) = 8 + 2 = 10; forgetting that integrating x⁻² produces a minus sign would give the wrong antiderivative.

questions.stem: What is the minimum value of x² + 16/x for x > 0?
questions.explanation: The derivative is 2x − 16/x², which vanishes when x³ = 8, so x = 2. It changes from negative to positive there, giving minimum value 4 + 8 = 12; 2 is where the minimum occurs, not its value.

questions.stem: For x > 0, x^(7/6)/√x equals the cube root of 16. Find x.
questions.explanation: Subtract exponents to get x^(2/3) = 16^(1/3). Cubing gives x² = 16, and the positive restriction selects 4.

questions.stem: The polynomial 2x³ − kx + c leaves the same remainder at x + 2 and x − 1. It is divisible by x − 2. Find c.
questions.explanation: Equal remainders give −16 + 2k + c = 2 − k + c, hence k = 6. Evaluating at x = 2 gives 16 − 12 + c = 0.

questions.stem: Let f(x) = 2x + 7 and g(x) = x². Find the solution to g(f(x)) = 25 for which f(x) is negative.
questions.explanation: The inner value can be 5 or −5. The negative branch gives 2x + 7 = −5, so x = −6.

questions.stem:
Let x² − 10x + k = 0 with k real. Which statements are correct?

1. Its roots coincide at k = 25.

2. It has no real roots at k = 26.

3. At k = 16 the roots differ by 4.
questions.explanation: The discriminant is 100 − 4k, zero at 25 and negative above. At k = 16 the roots are 2 and 8, a difference of 6.
Multiply top and bottom by √7 + √3. The denominator is 4 and the numerator is 10 + 2√21, including the cross term.

questions.stem: Solve y = 2x + 1 and y = x² − 2. Which row gives the sum; the product of the two x-values?
questions.explanation: Equating gives x² − 2x − 3 = 0, with x = −1 and 3. The y-values are not the roots being added and multiplied.

questions.stem: For which x does (x − 1)/(x + 2) < 0?
questions.explanation: For x ≠ −2, multiplying by the positive square (x + 2)² gives (x − 1)(x + 2) < 0. The upward-opening quadratic is negative strictly between its roots.

questions.stem: A monic cubic has roots 1 and −2. Its x² coefficient is −4. Which row gives its third root; its constant term?
questions.explanation: The roots sum to 4, so the third is 4 − 1 + 2 = 5. The constant is the negative product of the three roots.

questions.stem: For what value of k is f(f(x)) = 9x + 12 for all x, where f(x) = 3x + k?
questions.explanation: Composition multiplies the inner constant by 3, then adds another k. The total constant is 4k, not k².

questions.stem: A sign diagram is used to solve (x + 2)/(x² − 9) ≤ 0. Which intervals, together, describe the solution?
questions.explanation: The denominator is positive outside (−3, 3) and negative inside it, and x = ±3 is excluded. The numerator switches from negative to positive at −2, where the fraction is zero. The fraction is therefore nonpositive exactly for x < −3 or −2 ≤ x < 3.

questions.stem: An arithmetic sequence has third term 8 and sixth term 20. What is the smallest n for which Sₙ > 110?
questions.explanation: The common difference is 4 and the first term is zero. Thus Sₙ = 2n(n − 1); S₇ = 84 and S₈ = 112.

questions.stem: A convergent geometric series starts 18, −6, 2, … . How much larger is its sum to infinity than the sum of its first four terms?
questions.explanation: The tail starts at 18(−1/3)⁴ = 2/9 and has the same ratio −1/3. Its sum is (2/9)/(4/3) = 1/6, not just the first omitted term.

questions.stem: Find the coefficient of x in (3 − x)⁵.
questions.explanation: Choose −x in one of the five factors and 3 in the others. This gives −5 × 3⁴, not −3⁵.

questions.stem:
Let u₁ = 2 and uₙ₊₁ = 3uₙ − 4. Which statements are correct?

1. Every term is positive.

2. The sequence grows without bound.

3. The first two terms are equal.
questions.explanation: Substituting 2 into the recurrence returns 2, so every term equals 2. A multiplier greater than 1 does not force divergence from a fixed point.

questions.stem: The second and fourth terms of a geometric sequence are 6 and 24. Its common ratio is negative. Find its third term.
questions.explanation: The terms two steps apart have ratio 4, so the negative common ratio is −2. Multiplying the second term by +2 would not give the prescribed sign.

questions.stem: An arithmetic sequence starts 4, 7, 10, … . Which row gives its tenth term; the sum of its first ten terms?
questions.explanation: Add nine steps of 3 to the initial 4. The mean of the first and tenth terms is 17.5, and ten times that mean is 175.

questions.stem: Let v₁ = 5 and vₙ₊₁ = vₙ + 2n. Find v₅.
questions.explanation: The four increments from v₁ to v₅ are 2, 4, 6 and 8. Including the fifth increment would instead reach v₆.

questions.stem: For (1 − 3x)⁴, which row gives the coefficients of x²; x³?
questions.explanation: The coefficients are 6(−3)² and 4(−3)³. The sign alternates because the exponent of −3 changes parity.

questions.stem: The first three terms of a geometric sequence sum to 7 and the next three sum to 56. Find its first term.
questions.explanation: Moving each of the first three terms forward three places multiplies its value by r³, so r³ = 8. The first three then sum to a(1 + 2 + 4), giving a = 1.

questions.stem: The sum of the first n terms of 2, 5, 8, … exceeds 100. Find the least such n.
questions.explanation: Eight terms sum to 100 exactly, and nine sum to 126. The inequality is strict, so n = 8 is not enough.

questions.stem: An indicator travels anticlockwise around a unit circle from the point (1, 0). It turns through 5π/6 radians. What is its vertical coordinate?
questions.explanation: The vertical coordinate is sin(5π/6). Its reference angle is π/6, and sine is positive there, so the coordinate is 1/2.

questions.stem: Two sectors have equal perimeter. The first has radius 8 and angle 3/4 radians; the second has radius 6. Find the angle of the second in radians.
questions.explanation: The first perimeter is 16 + 8(3/4) = 22. Subtract the second sector’s two radii to get arc length 10, then divide by 6.

questions.stem: If cos θ = 3/5 and θ is acute, find tan θ.
questions.explanation: The sine is 4/5 from the identity, positive for acute θ. Divide sine by cosine, not the reverse.

questions.stem:
On 0 ≤ x < 2π, consider sin x = −1/2. Which statements are correct?

1. The solutions differ by π.

2. Both solutions lie above π.

3. One solution is 11π/6.
questions.explanation: The two angles are 7π/6 and 11π/6. Both exceed π, but their difference is 2π/3, not π.

questions.stem: A triangle has sides 5 and 8 enclosing an angle of 150°. Find its area.
questions.explanation: The area is ½ × 5 × 8 × sin 150° = 10. The obtuse angle has the same sine as its supplementary acute angle.

questions.stem: A sector has arc length 9 and radius 6. Which row gives its central angle (radians); its area?
questions.explanation: The angle is 9/6. The area is half radius times arc length, ½ × 6 × 9; the full rectangle product is twice too large.

questions.stem: On the graph y = f(x), the point (3, 7) lies on the curve. Which point must lie on y = f(x − 4) + 2?
questions.explanation: Use x − 4 = 3 to match the original input, then increase the output by 2. The horizontal shift is right, not left.

questions.stem: For sin θ = −3/5 and cos θ > 0, which row gives tan θ; cos(2θ)?
questions.explanation: Cosine is positive and equals 4/5. Tangent is −3/4 and cos(2θ) = cos²θ − sin²θ = 7/25, which is positive.

questions.stem: A student solving 2 sin x cos x = cos x on 0 ≤ x < 2π divides both sides by cos x. Which solution set is lost by this step?
questions.explanation: Dividing by cos x discards cases where cos x = 0. These are π/2 and 3π/2 in the interval, and at both points the original equation reads 0 = 0.

questions.stem: Triangle ABC has AB = BC = 6 and ∠ABC = 120°. Find AC.
questions.explanation: By the cosine rule AC² = 36 + 36 − 72cos 120° = 108. Cosine is negative, so the cross term increases the squared length.

questions.stem: Two functions R and S have derivatives R′(x) = 6x and S′(x) = 6x + 4. They have the same value at x = 1. Which expression gives S(x) − R(x)?
questions.explanation: The derivative of S − R is 4, so S − R = 4x + C. At x = 1 the difference vanishes, so C = −4.

questions.stem: The integral of 3x² + 1 from 0 to 2 is 10. Find the integral of 3x² − 2 from 1 to 2.
questions.explanation: The integral of 3x² + 1 from 0 to 1 is 2, leaving 8 from 1 to 2. Subtract 3 for the integrand change over this width-one interval.

questions.stem: The tangent to y = kx³ at x = 2 has gradient 24. Find k.
questions.explanation: The gradient is 3kx², which is 12k at x = 2. Setting the curve’s height, rather than the gradient, to 24 would give the wrong k.

questions.stem:
Between x = 0 and x = 1, consider y = x² and y = x. Which statements are correct?

1. The curves agree at both endpoints.

2. The parabola lies above the line inside the interval.

3. The enclosed area is 1/6.
questions.explanation: The curves meet at 0 and 1. Inside this interval x² < x, so integrate x − x² to obtain 1/2 − 1/3 = 1/6.

questions.stem: Given y′ = 4x − 3 and y(2) = 7, find y(0).
questions.explanation: Integration gives y = 2x² − 3x + C. At x = 2 the first two terms give 2, so C = 5 rather than 7.

questions.stem: Use two equal trapezia on 0 ≤ x ≤ 4 for y = x². Which row gives the estimate; the exact area?
questions.explanation: With strip width 2, the estimate is 0 + 2(4) + 16 = 24. The exact integral is 4³/3; halving the weighted sum again forgets the width.

questions.stem: For y = x³ − 12x, find the y-coordinate of its local maximum.
questions.explanation: The stationary points are at x = ±2. The second derivative is negative at −2, where the value is 16; x = 2 locates the minimum.

questions.stem: If ∫₀³ f(x) dx = 11 and ∫₁³ f(x) dx = 7, which row gives ∫₀¹ f(x) dx; ∫₀¹ (3f(x) + 2) dx?
questions.explanation: Subtract the integral over [1,3] from the one over [0,3]. On the remaining interval of width 1, multiplying by 3 and adding the constant contribution yields 14.

questions.stem: What area is enclosed by y = 6x − x² and y = 2x?
questions.explanation: The curves meet at x = 0 and 4. Between them, the vertical gap is 4x − x², whose integral is [2x² − x³/3] from 0 to 4, or 32/3. Integrating the parabola alone includes area below the straight line.

questions.stem: For x > 0, y′ = 2x + 6/x² and y(1) = −2. Find y(3).
questions.explanation: Integrating gives y = x² − 6/x + C. The initial value makes C = 3, and substituting x = 3 gives 9 − 2 + 3; the reciprocal term needs a minus sign.

questions.stem: A square has area 2¹² cm². A cube has volume 2¹² cm³. The side length of the square is how many times the side length of the cube?
questions.explanation: The square root gives side 2⁶ cm and the cube root gives side 2⁴ cm. Their ratio is 2² = 4.

questions.stem: Simplify (√6 − √2)².
questions.explanation: The cross term is −2√12 = −4√3. The two squares add to 8.

questions.stem: A monic quadratic has minimum value −4 at x = 3. For how many integers k does y = k cut it at two points with integer x-coordinates in [0, 6]?
questions.explanation: The curve is (x − 3)² − 4. The two distinct integer positions must be symmetric at distance 1, 2 or 3 from x = 3.

questions.stem: The roots of x³ − 4x² + ax + b are −1, 2 and r. Which row gives a; b?
questions.explanation: The roots sum to 4, so r = 3. Pairwise products sum to −2 − 3 + 6 = 1; the constant is minus the product of all three roots, so it is +6.

questions.stem: Find all real x satisfying x² − 4x < −3 and x² ≥ 2x.
questions.explanation: The first gives 1 < x < 3. The second gives x ≤ 0 or x ≥ 2, so only the part from 2 up to 3 remains.

questions.stem: If x + y = 4 and x³ + y³ = 28, find (x − y)².
questions.explanation: Expanding (x + y)³ gives 64 = 28 + 12xy, so xy = 3. Then (x − y)² = 16 − 12 = 4.

questions.stem: For how many integers k does x⁴ − 6x² + k = 0 have four distinct real roots?
questions.explanation: Set t = x²; two distinct positive t-values are needed. Their sum is 6 and product k, and the discriminant is 36 − 4k, so 0 < k < 9.

questions.stem: A monic cubic is divisible by x² − 1 and leaves remainder 15 on division by x − 2. What remainder does it leave on division by x + 3?
questions.explanation: Write it as (x² − 1)(x + a). At x = 2 the value is 3(2 + a) = 15, so a = 3. Evaluating at −3 now gives zero.

questions.stem: For g(x) = √(x + 1), at how many real x is g(g(x)) equal to √3?
questions.explanation: The outer square root returns √3 only when its input is 3, so √(x + 1) = 2. The solution x = 3 lies in the domain of both roots.

questions.stem: How many integer x satisfy 1 ≤ ∣x² − 9∣ < 9?
questions.explanation: The upper bound gives 0 < x² < 18. The lower excludes x² = 9, leaving x = ±1, ±2, ±4.

questions.stem: An arithmetic sequence has six terms, all positive, with last term 23. The terms add to 108. What is the first term?
questions.explanation: The mean of the six terms is 108 ÷ 6 = 18, also the mean of the two end terms. So the first term is 36 − 23 = 13.

questions.stem: A sequence has uₙ = n² − 4n. Which index gives the smallest term?
questions.explanation: Complete the square to get (n − 2)² − 4. The minimum is at index 2, not at the index where the term becomes zero.

questions.stem: Three consecutive terms of an increasing arithmetic sequence sum to 30 and their squares sum to 318. What is its common difference?
questions.explanation: The middle term is 10. The squares of 10 − d, 10 and 10 + d sum to 300 + 2d², so d = 3, taking the positive value.

questions.stem: An infinite geometric series starts 12, 6, … . Delete every third term. Find the sum of what remains.
questions.explanation: The full sum is 24. Deleted terms start at 3 with ratio 1/8, so subtract 24/7 rather than subtracting every other term.

questions.stem: In (1 + ax)⁶ the coefficient of x² is 60 and a is negative. Find the coefficient of x³.
questions.explanation: The x² coefficient is 15a², so a = −2. The next coefficient is 20a³, which is negative.

questions.stem: In an arithmetic sequence, terms 1–4 sum to 10 and terms 5–8 sum to 42. Which row gives the first term; the sum of terms 3–10?
questions.explanation: The later block adds 32, or 8 per term across four gaps, so d = 2. Then 4a + 12 = 10, and terms 3–10 sum to eight times their mean 10.5.

questions.stem: For a real sequence, u₁ > 3 and uₙ₊₁ = (uₙ + 6)/3. What can be proved about the difference uₙ − 3?

options.label: A
options.text: It stays positive and it decreases by 3 at every step.

options.label: B
options.text: It stays positive and it is multiplied by 3 at every step.

options.label: C
options.text: It changes sign and its magnitude is divided by 3 at every step.

options.label: D
options.text: It stays positive and it is divided by 3 at every step.

options.label: E
options.text: It reaches zero after exactly three steps.

questions.explanation: Subtract 3 from the recurrence to get uₙ₊₁ − 3 = (uₙ − 3)/3. Since the first difference is positive, every subsequent difference is positive and one third as large as the previous one.

questions.stem: In (2 + x)⁶(1 + bx), the x² coefficient is zero. Find the x³ coefficient.
questions.explanation: The x and x² coefficients of the first factor are 192 and 240. Cancellation requires b = −5/4; the x³ coefficient is 160 + 240b = −140.

questions.stem: A decreasing positive geometric sequence has first two terms summing to 18 and all terms summing to 24. Find its third term.
questions.explanation: The tail after two terms sums to 6, one quarter of the whole sum. Thus r² = 1/4, r = 1/2, and the third term is 6(1 − r).

questions.stem: Let (1 + x)⁴(1 − x)³ = 1 + x + ax² + bx³ + … . Which pair is (a, b)?
questions.explanation: Rewrite it as (1 + x)(1 − x²)³. The coefficient of x² is −3, and multiplication by x gives the same coefficient for x³.

questions.stem: A line from the origin has length 2 and makes an angle π/3 with the positive x-axis. What is the x-coordinate of its other endpoint?
questions.explanation: Its horizontal projection has length 2 cos(π/3) = 2 × 1/2 = 1.

questions.stem: A sector of radius 4 has area 6. Find its central angle in radians.
questions.explanation: Use A = r²θ/2, so θ = 2A/r². Arc length divided by radius works only if the arc length is given.

questions.stem: Sides a and b of a triangle have lengths 3 and 5. The enclosed angle has cosine −1/5. Find the square of the third side’s length.
questions.explanation: The cosine rule gives 9 + 25 − 2(3)(5)(−1/5) = 40. Subtracting a negative cross term increases the result.

questions.stem: Let sin θ = 4/5 and π/2 < θ < π. Which row gives tan θ; sin(2θ)?
questions.explanation: Cosine is −3/5 in quadrant II. Both sin θ/cos θ and 2sin θ cos θ are negative, giving the stated values.

questions.stem: How many solutions does 2sin²x − 3sin x + 1 = 0 have for 0 < x < 3π?
questions.explanation: The sine values are 1 and 1/2. Each occurs on two positive arches in the interval, once per arch for 1 and twice for 1/2.

questions.stem: The zeros of f are −2, 1 and 4. One zero of f(k − x) is 7, and the largest zero is 10. Find k.
questions.explanation: The largest transformed zero comes from the smallest original input, −2, so k + 2 = 10. The other zeros are 7 and 4, which checks the condition.

questions.stem: A triangle has sides 7, 8 and 13. Find its area.
questions.explanation: The angle between 7 and 8 has cosine (49 + 64 − 169)/112 = −1/2, hence sine √3/2. The area is 14√3.

questions.stem: For 0 ≤ x < 2π, how many solutions to cos(2x) = cos x have 0 < sin x?
questions.explanation: Writing c = cos x gives 2c² − c − 1 = 0, so c = 1 or −1/2. Only 2π/3 among the candidate angles has positive sine.

questions.stem: An arc and its chord both connect A and B on a circle of radius 6. The minor arc has length 4π. Which row gives the chord length; the minor sector area?
questions.explanation: The arc gives angle 2π/3, so half the chord is 6sin(π/3) = 3√3. The sector area is half the radius times the arc length.
Both terms contain 3^(2x) = 4. Their remaining multipliers are 9 and 1/3, so the difference is 4(9 − 1/3).

sets.title: Area, rates of change and constants

questions.stem: For every x, a function F has derivative x³. The function G is defined by G(x) = F(x) + 5. Which is an expression for G(x) − G(0)?
questions.explanation: The added 5 cancels in the difference. An antiderivative of x³ is x⁴/4 plus a constant, and subtracting its value at zero removes the constant.

questions.stem: Find the derivative of 4√x for x > 0.
questions.explanation: Write 4x^(1/2). Differentiating halves the coefficient and gives exponent −1/2.

questions.stem: The curve y = x² − 1 and the x-axis enclose a finite region. What is half its area?
questions.explanation: The enclosed region lies below the axis from −1 to 1. By symmetry half its area is the integral of 1 − x² from 0 to 1.

questions.stem: For a > 0, the integral of 3x² from a to 2a is 56. Find a.
questions.explanation: The integral equals (2a)³ − a³ = 7a³. Divide before taking the cube root and use both limits.

questions.stem: The tangent to y = x² at x = a passes through (0, −9). What is the sum of the squares of the possible a-values?
questions.explanation: The tangent is y = 2ax − a², so a² = 9. Both a = 3 and a = −3 contribute 9.

questions.stem: The integrals of f on [0, 2] and [1, 3] are 10 and 14. Its integral on [0, 3] is 18. Which row gives the integrals on [1, 2]; [2, 3]?
questions.explanation: The first two ranges count the overlap twice, giving overlap 10 + 14 − 18 = 6. The integral on [2, 3] is the whole minus the [0, 2] part, or 8.

questions.stem: Which value equals the signed integral of 1 − 4/x² from 1 to 4?
questions.explanation: The antiderivative x + 4/x has the same value at 1 and 4. Signed contributions can cancel even when the geometric area is not zero.

questions.stem: Use two equal trapezia on [0, 2] for y = ax² + 3 with a > 0. The estimate exceeds the exact area by 2. Find a.
questions.explanation: The constant is integrated exactly by the trapezia. For x² the estimate is 3 and the integral is 8/3, so the excess is a/3.

questions.stem: For x > 0, y = x + k/x has minimum 8. Which row gives the minimising x; k?
questions.explanation: At a stationary point, k = x². Then y = x + x = 8, giving x = 4 and k = 16. The derivative changes from negative to positive there.

questions.stem: Let F(x) = ∫₁ˣ (t² − 4) dt. At what positive x does the graph of F have a horizontal tangent?
questions.explanation: By the fundamental theorem, F′(x) = x² − 4. Use the positive zero of this derivative; the lower integration limit is not involved.

questions.stem: For positive x, let A = x^(1/2) and B = x^(1/3). Which equation holds for every positive x?
questions.explanation: Squaring the square root and cubing the cube root both give x.

questions.stem: Which of x − 1, x + 1, x − 2 and x + 2 is a factor of x³ − 3x + 2 if the factor must be repeated?
questions.explanation: The cubic is (x − 1)²(x + 2), so only x − 1 is repeated. A zero test alone would also find the simple factor x + 2.

questions.stem: Given log₂ 6 = a, express log₂ 12 in terms of a.
questions.explanation: Since 12 = 2 × 6, add log₂ 2 = 1. The product rule adds logs rather than multiplying the value of a.

questions.stem: Which exact expression equals 3/(√5 + 2) + 1/(√5 − 2)?
questions.explanation: The conjugate product is 5 − 4 = 1. The two fractions become 3(√5 − 2) and √5 + 2, whose rational terms sum to −4.

questions.stem: For real x and y, x² + y² = 25 and x + y = 7. Which row gives xy; ∣x − y∣?
questions.explanation: Squaring the sum gives 49 = 25 + 2xy. Subtract 2xy from 25 to obtain (x − y)² = 1.
Use 4^(x+1) = (2 × 2^x)² = 36. The denominator is 3 + 1, not 3 squared plus 1.

questions.stem: For which value of k do y = x² − 4x + 7 and y = 2x + k touch?
questions.explanation: At intersection, x² − 6x + 7 − k = 0. A repeated root requires 7 − k = 9, yielding k = −2.

questions.stem: How many integers x make both x² ≤ 36 and (x + 1)(x − 4) ≥ 0 true?
questions.explanation: The first interval is [−6, 6]. The second includes x ≤ −1 or x ≥ 4, giving six integers on the left and three on the right.

questions.stem: A monic cubic has roots −2 and 3 and leaves remainder 8 at x = 0. Find the sum of its three roots.
questions.explanation: Write it as (x + 2)(x − 3)(x − r). Its constant term is 6r = 8, so the sum is −2 + 3 + 4/3.

questions.stem: For x > 1, log₂(x − 1) + log₂(x + 2) = 3. Find x.
questions.explanation: Combine logs to get (x − 1)(x + 2) = 8. This gives x² + x − 10 = 0, and only the positive-root branch satisfies x > 1.

questions.stem: A sequence is given by uₙ = n(n + 2) for n = 1, 2, 3, …. Which expression gives uₙ₊₁ − uₙ?
questions.explanation: The next term is (n + 1)(n + 3). Subtracting n(n + 2) gives 2n + 3.

questions.stem: The first seven terms of an arithmetic sequence sum to 63. What is the fourth term?
questions.explanation: The fourth term is the mean of the seven terms by symmetry. Divide the sum by seven.

questions.stem: What is the sign of sin x cos x at x = 2π/3?
questions.explanation: Sine is positive and cosine negative in quadrant II. Multiplying numbers of opposite sign gives a negative value.

questions.stem: A circle has radius 5. Find the length of the arc subtending 2π/5 at its centre.
questions.explanation: Arc length is radius times the angle in radians. The given angle is only one fifth of a full turn.

questions.stem: A positive geometric series begins 4, 2, 1. Express its fifth term as a fraction of its sum to infinity.
questions.explanation: The fifth term is 4(1/2)⁴ = 1/4, while the sum is 8. Divide the term by the sum.

questions.stem: Two arithmetic sequences start 4, 9, 14, … and 7, 10, 13, … . What is the smallest number belonging to both?
questions.explanation: The first sequence has 4, 9, 14, 19; the second has 7, 10, 13, 16, 19. The smallest intersection is 19.

questions.stem: For (1 + 2x)⁶, what is the ratio of the coefficient of x² to that of x⁴?
questions.explanation: The binomial factors are both 15. Their powers of 2 give a ratio of 4 to 16, not 1 to 1.

questions.stem: For acute angles A and B, sin A = 3/5 and sin B = 4/5. Which row gives cos A; A + B?
questions.explanation: The two sine values are each the other angle’s cosine. In the acute range the angles are complementary, so they sum to π/2.

questions.stem: How many solutions of sin(2x) = cos x lie in 0 ≤ x < 2π?
questions.explanation: Factor cos x(2sin x − 1) = 0. Cosine is zero at two angles and sine is 1/2 at two other angles. Dividing by cosine would lose half the solutions.

questions.stem: Triangle ABC has ∠A = 30°, BC = 4 and AC = 4√2. Which row gives the two possible values of ∠C?
questions.explanation: The sine rule gives sin B = √2/2, so B is 45° or 135°. Subtract B and 30° from 180° rather than reporting the possible B angles.

questions.stem: A student differentiates y = 7x² − 5 and gets the same gradient at x = −2 as at x = 2. Which correction should they make?

options.label: B
options.text: The gradient at x = −2 should be 4 more than at x = 2.

options.label: C
options.text: The gradient at x = −2 is the negative of the gradient at x = 2.

options.label: E
options.text: The gradients should be equal because both x-values give the same y.

questions.explanation: The derivative is 14x, so replacing x by −x reverses the sign of the gradient. Equal heights do not imply equal gradients.

questions.stem: The areas under y = 3x² between x = 0 and x = 1, and between x = 1 and x = 2, are A and B respectively. What is B/A?
questions.explanation: The antiderivative is x³. Thus A = 1 and the area up to x = 2 is 8. The second area is 8 − 1 = 7, giving B/A = 7.

questions.stem: At x = 4 the graph of f has derivative −3. Which description follows for the tangent there?

options.label: D
options.text: It slopes downwards as x increases.

questions.explanation: A negative derivative means a negative tangent slope. The derivative alone does not specify the intercept or height.

questions.stem: By how much does a function with derivative 6x + 1 change from x = −1 to x = 1?
questions.explanation: An antiderivative is 3x² + x. Between −1 and 1 its quadratic part cancels and its linear part rises by 2.

questions.stem: The integral of f from −2 to 3 is 11 and that of g is 4. Which row gives the integrals of 2f − g; f − 2g on the same interval?
questions.explanation: Linearity gives 2×11 − 4 = 18 and 11 − 2×4 = 3. Each multiplier acts only on its own function.

questions.stem: The heights of y = f(x) at x = 0, 3, 6 are 2, k and 4. The two-strip trapezium estimate is 30. Find k.
questions.explanation: The width is 3, so the weighted sum satisfies 3(2 + 2k + 4)/2 = 30. The middle height contributes twice.

questions.stem: A normal to y = x² at x = 1 crosses the x-axis at P. Find the distance from P to (1, 0).
questions.explanation: At (1, 1) the normal slope is −1/2. Dropping one unit to the axis requires two units horizontally; the x-intercept is 3.

questions.stem: The curve y = 3x − x² lies above the x-axis between its two roots. Which row gives its enclosed area; its maximum height?
questions.explanation: The roots are 0 and 3, and integration gives 27/2 − 9 = 9/2. The midpoint x = 3/2 gives maximum height 9/4.

questions.stem: Let F(x) = ∫₀ˣ (t² − 1) dt. What is the area between y = F′(x) and the x-axis for 0 ≤ x ≤ 2?
questions.explanation: Since F′(x) = x² − 1, split at x = 1. The signed integral from 0 to 1 is −2/3 and from 1 to 2 is 4/3; add their magnitudes.

questions.stem: For y = x³ − 3x² − 24x, find the difference between its local maximum and local minimum heights.
questions.explanation: The derivative factors as 3(x − 4)(x + 2). The heights at −2 and 4 are 28 and −80; their difference is 108.

questions.stem: A circle has centre (3, −2) and touches the x-axis. What is its equation?
questions.explanation: Its radius is 2, the vertical distance from the centre to the x-axis. The right side in the circle equation is the square of the radius.

questions.stem: Which gradient is perpendicular to that of a line through (0, 2) and (4, 4)?
questions.explanation: The given gradient is 1/2. Its negative reciprocal is −2, not −1/2.

questions.stem: The graph y = f(x) passes through (2, −3). What is the y-coordinate of y = −2f(x) at x = 2?
questions.explanation: Multiply the output at the same x by −2. A vertical transformation does not move the point horizontally.

questions.stem: The integral of f from 1 to 4 is 9. What is the integral of f from 4 to 1?
questions.explanation: Reversing limits reverses the sign of the definite integral, not its absolute magnitude.

questions.stem: The tangent to x² + y² = 25 at (3, 4) meets the y-axis at Q. Find the y-coordinate of Q.
questions.explanation: The radius has slope 4/3, so the tangent slope is −3/4. Setting x = 0 in y − 4 = −3(x − 3)/4 gives 25/4.

questions.stem: For how many positive integer k does y = k meet the graph y = ∣x² − 5∣ at four distinct points?
questions.explanation: Both x² = 5 + k and x² = 5 − k must have two distinct real solutions. The latter requires k < 5; equality gives one repeated solution.

questions.stem: The graph y = f(x) has a unique maximum at (−3, 7). Which row is the maximum point of y = 2f(3 − x) − 4? Give x; y.
questions.explanation: The maximum occurs where the function’s input 3 − x equals −3. Its output is transformed to 2×7 − 4 = 10.

questions.stem: Evaluate ∫₀¹ x(x + 2)² dx.
questions.explanation: Expand to x³ + 4x² + 4x. The integral is 1/4 + 4/3 + 2 = 43/12; the square includes the middle term.

questions.stem: A circle has diameter endpoints (−1, 2) and (5, 10). Which row gives its centre; the length of its chord on x = 5?
questions.explanation: The centre is the midpoint and the radius is half of 10. The chord lies three units from the centre, so its half-length is √(25 − 9) = 4.

questions.stem: A curve has gradient 6x − 6 and is tangent to y = 6x + 1. Find the curve’s minimum height.
questions.explanation: Equal gradients give 6x − 6 = 6 at the contact, so x = 2 and y = 13. The minimum is at x = 1; integrating the gradient from 1 to 2 gives a height increase of 3. Thus the minimum is 10.
